log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Mega Scizor. Lead Grimmsnarl+Politoed: Prankster Fake Out (+3) flinches Venusaur before Chlorophyll sun speed matters, Politoed Ice Beam (2x SE) breaks Focus Sash. Screens go up T2. Scizor-Mega switches in under screens; Bullet Punch picks off 1-HP Venusaur; Close Combat hits Garchomp/Goodra. Archaludon cleans late with Electro Shot/Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor at most once. Cycle Politoed to re-establish rain after Drought override.
decisions.notebook: Opp consistently brings Zard-Y+Venusaur+Garchomp+Raichu. Venusaur=Focus Sash+Chlorophyll, real wincon under sun. Zard-Y Mega Evolves T1 for Drought, spams Flamethrower. Garchomp uses Stomping Tantrum (150 BP if prev move failed). Raichu=Fake Out+Lightning Rod support. Opp double-targets aggressively. Scizor-Mega 4x Fire weak needs screens before switching in. Archaludon must avoid double Draco Meteor or becomes useless late. Game 3 plan: lead Grimmsnarl+Politoed for screens+rain, break Venusaur Sash with priority before sun setup, save Archaludon for late cleanup with intact SpA, Draco Meteor at most once.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega is Charizard Y. Lead Charizard-Venusaur establishes sun, denying Politoed’s rain and making Venusaur immediately fast for Sleep Powder while Charizard pressures Scizor and Grimmsnarl. Garchomp is the direct Archaludon answer with guaranteed Stomping Tantrum pressure; Hisuian Goodra gives a resilient Steel/Dragon endgame and threatens Archaludon with Body Press or Scizor with sun-boosted Fire Blast.

Fake Out (+3 pri) flinches Venusaur before Sleep Powder and breaks Focus Sash. Ice Beam chips 29-62% SE, leaving Venu at 28-66% with Sash gone—KOable T2 by Bullet Punch+Ice Beam. Politoed survives Zard-Y Flamethrower (17-35%). Solar Beam risk (62-126%) exists but opp favors Flamethrower per tendencies.
decisions.notebook:
Game 3 plan: lead Grimmsnarl+Politoed for screens+rain, break Venusaur Sash with priority before sun setup, save Archaludon for late cleanup with intact SpA, Draco Meteor at most once.

Opp tendencies: Zard-Y megas T1 for Drought, spams Flamethrower. Garchomp uses Stomping Tantrum (150 BP if prev move failed). Raichu=Fake Out+Lightning Rod support. Opp double-targets aggressively, rarely Protects.

Key damage calcs (Gen9 L50 doubles): Politoed Ice Beam→Venusaur 29-62% (SE2x). Zard-Y Flamethrower→Politoed 17-35% (NVE, survives). Zard-Y Solar Beam→Politoed 62-126% (possible KO). Scizor-Mega Bullet Punch→Venusaur 16.6-37.4% (Technician+STAB).

T2 plan after Fake Out+Ice Beam T1: switch Grimmsnarl→Scizor-Mega, Bullet Punch(+1 pri) KOs chipped Venusaur before Sleep Powder. Politoed Ice Beam as backup if awake. Scizor 4x Fire weak under sun—likely trades for Venusaur. Acceptable: removes sun wincon, Archaludon cleans late.

If opp Solar Beams Politoed T1 and KOs it: lose Drizzle+Ice Beam, must rely on Scizor priority+Archaludon. Consider switching Politoed out T2 to reset Drizzle rain (overrides Drought) if Venusaur is already KO'd.

decisions.rationale: Mega Protect immediately replaces rain with sun while denying the most direct Fake Out/Hydro Pump line into Charizard. Venusaur is then faster under Chlorophyll and can put Grimmsnarl to sleep before it establishes screens if it does not Fake Out Venusaur. This preserves both attackers and gives the strongest next-turn Politoed removal line.

Both foes outspeed us, so we eat their hits first. Double-targeting Venusaur (33% HP) with Spirit Break (11.8-26.5%) + Ice Beam (28.9-61.9%) guarantees the KO if both land and covers Ice Beam low-rolls (~12% miss-to-KO). Removing the Chlorophyll sweeper is the series-deciding priority. Keeping Scizor benched avoids a 4x sun Fire OHKO on switch-in. If one mon is Slept/KO'd, the other still likely finishes Venusaur.

Revised T2 decision: double-target Venusaur with Spirit Break+Ice Beam instead of switching to Scizor, to avoid 4x Fire OHKO on switch-in. If Venusaur KO'd, bring Scizor next turn for Bullet Punch priority vs Charizard or switch to Archaludon for late cleanup. If Venusaur survives (both attacks somehow blocked), reassess—consider Protect+switch plays.

decisions.rationale: Scizor is guaranteed OHKO under sun (4x Fire weak, 192-645%). Archaludon takes Fire neutrally, survives with Light Screen support (Flamethrower 24-83% through screens), tanks Garchomp Rock Slide (NVE 3.6-10.9%), and can OHKO Garchomp with Draco Meteor (60-196.7% + Expert Belt). Grimmsnarl must set Prankster Light Screen next turn to keep Archaludon alive vs Charizard-Y. Scizor saved for post-sun cleanup only.
decisions.notebook:
Game 3 plan revised: Politoed fainted T2 (Leaf Storm crit). Venusaur KO'd T2. Sun active 4 turns (Charizard-Y Drought). Remaining: Grimmsnarl 57%, Archaludon 100%, Scizor 100%.

Key calcs: Char-Y Flamethrower vs Archaludon sun 48.7-166.1% (possible OHKO no screens; 24-83% with Light Screen). Char-Y Heat Wave spread vs Archaludon 38.6-130.9% (19-65% with screens). Char-Y Flamethrower vs Scizor 192-645% (guaranteed OHKO). Char-Y Flamethrower vs Grimmsnarl 44.1-145.3% (57% HP = KO range). Garchomp Rock Slide vs Archaludon 3.6-10.9% (NVE 0.5x, non-threat). Archaludon Draco Meteor vs Garchomp 60-196.7% (2x SE + Expert Belt, possible OHKO).

Plan: Send Archaludon now. Next turn Grimmsnarl Prankster Light Screen + Archaludon Protect. Then Archaludon attacks with screen support: Draco Meteor for Garchomp, Flash Cannon for neutral chip. Stall sun turns with Protect. Scizor only viable after sun expires (4 turns) if Char-Y doesn't re-enter.

Threat: Talonflame Gale Wings Brave Bird (+1 pri, Speed 160-195) outspeeds Grimmsnarl Prankster Light Screen (+1 pri, Speed 80) — could KO Grimmsnarl before screens. Raichu Fake Out on switch-in flinches Archaludon.

Opp tendencies: double-targets aggressively, rarely Protects. Zard-Y spams Flamethrower/Heat Wave under sun. Garchomp uses Stomping Tantrum (150 BP if prev move failed).

decisions.rationale: Double Grass pressure is the best route to remove Politoed through Prankster Light Screen before it can repeatedly threaten Venusaur or eventually reset rain. Charizard is guaranteed faster than Politoed, while Venusaur also acts before it; if Politoed attacks rather than Protects, both attacks connect before its move.
decisions.notebook: Archaludon will use Draco Meteor to remove Raichu rather than solely pursuing Electric pressure; Lightning Rod is not a dependable long-term answer. Opponent can establish both Light Clay screens even while Archaludon protects. Future plan: prioritize immediate Archaludon pressure with Garchomp/Charizard and preserve Venusaur to break Grimmsnarl or close after screens. Grimmsnarl has shown Fake Out pressure alongside Politoed Ice Beam; respect its Prankster screens when planning damage.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp gives the strongest immediate follow-up beside Charizard, with Stomping Tantrum, Rock Slide, and Dragon Claw covering likely incoming Steel-, Rock-, and Dragon-types. It also preserves Goodra-Hisui as a slower defensive endgame option.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Grimmsnarl has Fake Out plus Light Clay Prankster screens and can establish both screens. Politoed showed Ice Beam and Helping Hand. Archaludon has Draco Meteor, Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, and Protect; do not rely on Lightning Rod alone. Prioritize immediate pressure on Archaludon and deny or play around screens.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Archaludon)
decisions.rationale: Prankster Light Screen guarantees special defense buffer before any foe move; Protect keeps Archaludon at 100% while both foes likely waste attacks into Protect. Without screens Char-Y can OHKO Archaludon under sun. Next turn with LS active, Flamethrower drops to ~24-83% survivable range and Archaludon can Draco Meteor Garchomp or Electro Shot Char-Y. Sun ticks to 2 turns, stalling toward Scizor window.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 plan: T3 Light Screen + Protect. T4 with LS: Draco Meteor Garchomp (60-196.7% poss OHKO 2x SE+EBelt) or Electro Shot Char-Y (2x SE no STAB). Watch for Garchomp Stomping Tantrum 150BP if it hit Protect T3. Sun expires after T5 (3 turns from T3). Scizor enters only after sun ends — Char-Y Flamethrower guaranteed OHKO vs Scizor under sun. Grimmsnarl at 57% is in Flamethrower KO range (44-145%). If Grimmsnarl falls, LS persists 8 turns (Light Clay). Archaludon SpA drops 2 stages after Draco Meteor — plan follow-up with Electro Shot or switch. Opp: aggressive double-targeting, rarely Protects. Char-Y spams fire under sun. Garchomp Jolly LifeOrb 134-169 Spe.

decisions.rationale: Take the immediate double-KO line. Flamethrower is guaranteed to remove Grimmsnarl from its shown HP in sun, while Life Orb Stomping Tantrum is a guaranteed OHKO on Archaludon without Reflect. Screens or Protect are the material disruptions, but removing Grimmsnarl prevents further screen cycling and preserves the clearest endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Grimmsnarl: Prankster, Light Clay, Fake Out, Reflect, Light Screen, Spirit Break. Politoed: Drizzle, Sitrus Berry, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Helping Hand, Protect. Archaludon: Expert Belt, Stamina, Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Protect. Prioritize immediate Archaludon pressure and deny or play around Grimmsnarl screens.

decisions.rationale: Grimmsnarl Reflect via Prankster goes before all foe moves, halving Garchomp's 150BP Stomping Tantrum to ~37-76% so Archaludon survives. Archaludon then OHKOs Garchomp with Expert Belt Draco Meteor (~97-210%). Grimmsnarl dies to Flamethrower but Reflect+Light Screen are up for Scizor endgame. Opp rarely Protects so Draco Meteor landing is likely. Sun ends T6; Scizor enters safely then.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 plan: T4 Reflect+DracoMeteor->Garchomp. After T4 expect: Garchomp KO'd, Grimmsnarl KO'd, Archaludon ~24-63% HP with -2 SpA, Reflect(5t)+LScreen(6t) up, sun 1t left. Bring Scizor T5. Scizor MUST stay out of sun — Char-Y Flamethrower/HeatWave OHKOs under sun. Sun expires after T5 (2t from T3). Archaludon -2 SpA means Electro Shot/Flash Cannon much weaker; consider switching out or tanking with screens. Scizor-Mega Bullet Punch (priority Technician) is primary cleanup tool vs Char-Y and remaining foe. Opp 4th Pokemon unknown (Talonflame/Raichu/Goodra-Hisui). Raichu LightningRod blocks Electro Shot. Talonflame GaleWings BraveBird threatens Scizor. Goodra-Hisui SapSipper irrelevant vs our team. Opp tendencies: aggressive double-targeting, rarely Protects, Char-Y spams fire under sun.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Remove Grimmsnarl while insulating Garchomp from the likely Draco Meteor. A Prankster Reflect would otherwise halve Stomping Tantrum before it can KO Archaludon; preserving Garchomp lets it threaten the guaranteed Ground KO next turn after screens/Protect are navigated.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Grimmsnarl: Prankster, Light Clay, Fake Out, Reflect, Light Screen, Spirit Break. Politoed: Drizzle, Sitrus Berry, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Helping Hand, Protect. Archaludon: Expert Belt, Stamina, Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Protect. Prioritize immediate Archaludon pressure; respect Prankster Reflect before committing physical Ground damage. Charizard and Garchomp naturally outspeed revealed Archaludon range.

decisions.rationale: Scizor MUST Protect — Charizard's Flamethrower OHKOs through Light Screen under sun. Mega Evolve for free stats. Archaludon Electro Shots Charizard (Expert Belt ~46-146% = solid OHKO chance). Archaludon survives any double-target (Flamethrower neutral+Light Screen=24-83%, Garchomp physical halved by Reflect). Sun expires after T5. Next turn Scizor-Mega BPunches Garchomp (priority 180 eff) while Archaludon cleans up at full SpA. Avoid double Protect — opponent could switch in Raichu (LightningRod
decisions.notebook: Game 3 T5 plan: Scizor Protect+Mega, Archaludon Electro Shot→Charizard. After T5: sun gone, Scizor-Mega active at 100%, Archaludon likely 50-100%. T6: Scizor-Mega Bullet Punch→Garchomp (priority, STAB+Tech+SE=180eff), Archaludon Electro Shot→Charizard again or Draco Meteor→Garchomp if Charizard fainted. Key: Archaludon Draco Meteor was blocked by Protect T4 so NO -2 SpA drop — full 194 SpA intact. Scizor-Mega Bullet Punch is primary cleanup vs Garchomp (180 eff) but useless vs Charizard (22.5 eff). Archaludon must handle Charizard. Opp backline: Talonflame GaleWings BraveBird threatens Scizor 4x; Raichu LightningRod blocks Electro Shot; Goodra-Hisui SapSipper irrelevant. If opponent brings Raichu, avoid Electro Shot — use Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon instead. Opp tendencies: aggressive double-targeting, rarely Protects, Char-Y spams fire under sun.

decisions.rationale: Flamethrower is a guaranteed 4x OHKO on Scizor in sun and avoids Heat Wave accuracy. Garchomp always moves before Archaludon and pressures it with Life Orb STAB Ground; Reflect reduces the damage but Archaludon cannot safely gain momentum. Removing Scizor prevents it from exploiting Charizard while preserving immediate pressure.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed core: Grimmsnarl used Light Clay screens; Politoed has Drizzle, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Helping Hand, Protect; Archaludon has Expert Belt with Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Protect; Scizor has Scizorite and Bullet Punch/U-turn/Close Combat/Protect. Against screens, prioritize special Fire pressure into Scizor and avoid relying on physical KOs through Reflect. Garchomp naturally outspeeds revealed Archaludon range.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Both foes outspeed both my mons; Charizard Flamethrower is guaranteed OHKO on Scizor (4x SE). Bullet Punch chip (15-32%) is irrelevant—Draco Meteor OHKOs Garchomp regardless. Only win path is keeping Scizor alive: Protect (priority +4, 50% success) blocks Charizard's fire. If it works, T7 double threat forces Garchomp to choose: target Scizor→Archaludon Draco Meteors Garchomp for KO; target Archaludon→Scizor Close Combats. If Protect fails, I'm no worse off than Bullet Punch (Archaludon alone lo
decisions.notebook:
Archaludon +1 SpA Draco Meteor (2x SE STAB ExpertBelt, ~291 eff SpA) should OHKO Garchomp. Garchomp outspeeds Archaludon 134-169 vs 123.
Scizor-Mega Bullet Punch: 15-32% to Garchomp (neutral). Close Combat: higher but no priority, moves last vs both foes.
Charizard-Mega-Y Flamethrower: guaranteed OHKO Scizor (4x SE) even under Light Screen.
Garchomp Stomping Tantrum: ~22-44% to Archaludon (adjusted LifeOrb+Reflect+Def+1).
Opp backline: Talonflame GaleWings BraveBird 4x Scizor; Raichu LightningRod blocks Electro Shot; Goodra-Hisui SapSipper Steel/Dragon mirror. If Raichu active, use Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon not Electro Shot.
Win condition: keep both Scizor+Archaludon alive to force Garchomp target choice. If Garchomp targets Scizor, Archaludon Draco Meteors for KO.
Opp tendencies: aggressive double-targeting, rarely Protects, Char-Y spams fire.

decisions.rationale: Flamethrower cleanly removes Scizor through Light Screen, while Stomping Tantrum preserves pressure on Archaludon. Splitting avoids losing to an Archaludon Protect versus a double target line; Garchomp acts before Archaludon absent priority, and Goodra remains a strong endgame reserve.
Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Garchomp guaranteed outspeeds Archaludon (134-169 vs 123). At 5% HP any hit KOs. Draco Meteor cannot fire before Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum. Protect is the only line that survives this turn, buying one more turn for a potential opponent misplay. Game is near-lost but Protect maximizes remaining win equity.
decisions.notebook: Opp tendencies: aggressive double-targeting, rarely Protects, Char-Y spams fire. Garchomp Jolly LifeOrb 134-169 Speed. Goodra-Hisui Modest Leftovers 80-112 Speed SapSipper. Archaludon Modest ExpertBelt Stamina. Scizor-Mega Adamant Technician 105 Speed. Politoed Bold Sitrus Drizzle 90 Speed. Grimmsnarl Careful LightClay Prankster 80 Speed. Opp backline not brought: Talonflame Jolly MentalHerb GaleWings 160-195, Raichu Timid Sitrus LightningRod 143-178. Key speed tiers: Garchomp > Archaludon > Goodra. Raichu LightningRod blocks Electro Shot — use Draco Meteor/Flash Cannon if Raichu active. Goodra-Hisui Steel/Dragon resists all Archaludon STAB (0.5x); Fire Blast 2x SE vs Archaludon.

decisions.rationale: Body Press removes 4% Archaludon through its Defense boosts if it does not Protect. Garchomp Protect covers the only meaningful counterplay, boosted Draco Meteor, while Archaludon’s Steel and Electric attacks are resisted by Goodra-Hisui. If Archaludon Protects, both Pokémon remain positioned to finish it safely next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s revealed core: Grimmsnarl used Light Clay screens; Politoed has Drizzle, Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Helping Hand, Protect; Archaludon has Expert Belt with Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Protect and Stamina; Scizor has Scizorite and Bullet Punch/U-turn/Close Combat/Protect. Against screens, prioritize special Fire pressure into Scizor and avoid relying on physical KOs through Reflect. Garchomp naturally outspeeds revealed Archaludon range.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Archaludon at 5% is outsped by Garchomp who KOs with Stomping Tantrum before I can act. Protect is the only option with any survival chance. Even if it works, Garchomp KOs next turn, and all my STAB is 0.25-0.5x vs Goodra-Hisui. Game is nearly lost but Protect is the optimal play.
decisions.notebook: Opp tendencies: aggressive double-targeting, rarely Protects, Char-Y spams fire. Garchomp Jolly LifeOrb 134-169 Speed. Goodra-Hisui Modest Leftovers 80-112 Speed SapSipper Steel/Dragon. Archaludon Modest ExpertBelt Stamina. Scizor-Mega Adamant Technician 105 Speed. Politoed Bold Sitrus Drizzle 90 Speed. Grimmsnarl Careful LightClay Prankster 80 Speed. Opp backline not brought: Talonflame Jolly MentalHerb GaleWings 160-195, Raichu Timid Sitrus LightningRod 143-178. Key speed tiers: Garchomp > Archaludon > Goodra. Raichu LightningRod blocks Electro Shot. Goodra-Hisui Steel/Dragon resists all Archaludon STAB (0.25-0.5x); Fire Blast 2x SE vs Archaludon. Archaludon Draco Meteor +1 SpA + Expert Belt OHKOs 80% Garchomp but loses speed tie. Consider faster Archaludon spread or different coverage for Goodra-Hisui matchup in future games.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp outspeeds Archaludon and Stomping Tantrum is super effective; Archaludon is at 4%, so this is the cleanest immediate KO. Goodra’s Body Press covers a highly unlikely failure to KO if Archaludon does not Protect.

reflections.summary: Lost game 3 due to a poor team-preview matchup. Scizor-Mega (4x Fire-weak) was brought into a Charizard-Y sun team and fainted to one Flamethrower after Protect failed. Politoed's Drizzle was immediately overridden by Drought, rendering it low-value. Archaludon could not break Goodra-Hisui (resists all STABs) and was outsped and KO'd by Garchomp's SE Stomping Tantrum. Consecutive Protect failure on turn 8 sealed the loss, but the root cause was the four brought and the Mega choice not suiting th
reflections.adjustment: Against Charizard-Y sun cores, do not bring Scizor-Mega. Re-evaluate whether Politoed earns a slot when Drought overrides Drizzle. Prioritize bringing Pokémon that can answer Garchomp (speed control or Intimidate) and pressure Goodra-Hisui, since Archaludon alone cannot break it.
reflections.notebook: Opp tendencies: aggressive double-targeting, rarely Protects, Char-Y spams fire. Garchomp Jolly LifeOrb 134-169 Speed, runs Stomping Tantrum (SE vs Archaludon). Goodra-Hisui Modest Leftovers 80-112 Speed SapSipper Steel/Dragon, runs Body Press/Fire Blast/Flash Cannon/Protect; resists all Archaludon STAB (0.25-0.5x), Fire Blast 2x SE vs Archaludon. Venusaur Modest FocusSash Chlorophyll, runs Sleep Powder/Leaf Storm/Sludge Bomb/Protect. Opp backline not brought: Talonflame Jolly MentalHerb GaleWings 160-195, Raichu Timid Sitrus LightningRod 143-178. Key speed tiers: Garchomp > Archaludon > Goodra. Raichu LightningRod blocks Electro Shot. Scizor-Mega is a liability into Charizard-Y sun teams (4x Fire weak, OHKO'd by Flamethrower). Politoed Drizzle is overridden by Charizard-Y Drought — low value in that matchup. Archaludon Draco Meteor +1 SpA + Expert Belt OHKOs 80% Garchomp but loses speed tie. Consider faster Archaludon spread or different coverage for Goodra-Hisui matchup in future games. Plan: vs sun, drop Scizor-Mega and Politoed; bring answers to Garchomp speed and Goodra-Hisui typing.

reflections.summary: Won by removing Light Clay Grimmsnarl quickly, then using Garchomp’s repeated super-effective Stomping Tantrums to leave Archaludon in range for the Goodra-Hisui/Garchomp endgame. The Charizard-Y/Garchomp/Venusaur/Goodra-Hisui four and Mega Y were suitable: Charizard pressured both Grimmsnarl and Mega Scizor, while the backline handled Archaludon.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same general four and Mega Y plan, but once Archaludon has gained an Electro Shot boost, preserve Charizard rather than accepting a trade if possible; pivot to Goodra-Hisui/Garchomp to finish Archaludon while retaining Charizard’s Fire pressure.
reflections.notebook: Opponent favors Grimmsnarl Light Clay dual screens to support Archaludon and Mega Scizor. Archaludon is Expert Belt Stamina with Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, and Protect; it used Protect repeatedly while accumulating boosts. Mega Scizor carries Bullet Punch, U-turn, Close Combat, and Protect. Continue prioritizing early Grimmsnarl removal, use special Fire pressure on Scizor through Reflect, and use Garchomp plus Goodra-Hisui to close against Archaludon.
